notes: Official 2026 USMLE Blood/Lymphoreticular outline includes adverse reactions associated with transfused blood components.

Platelet Transfusion StatPearls last updated June 6, 2024 in the 2026 edition; posttransfusion purpura onset approximately 5–12 days after transfusion, severe thrombocytopenia, bleeding and platelet alloantibodies directly supported.

duplicate_gate.selected_construct: Post-transfusion purpura delayed severe alloimmune thrombocytopenia

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Previously sensitized multiparous woman develops abrupt profound isolated thrombocytopenia and mucocutaneous bleeding 7 days after transfusion: classic post-transfusion purpura.
adversarial_second_pass.ITP_attack: ITP can cause isolated thrombocytopenia, but the characteristic transfusion timing plus sensitization context makes PTP superior.
adversarial_second_pass.TTP_attack: No schistocytes or microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.
adversarial_second_pass.DIC_attack: Normal PT/aPTT/fibrinogen argues strongly against consumptive coagulopathy.
adversarial_second_pass.HIT_attack: No heparin exposure and the pattern is profound bleeding thrombocytopenia rather than typical HIT thrombosis/moderate fall.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
